source: CISA Bad Practices catalog, github.com/cisagov/bad-practices README, commit fd26f25 (2026-08-05)
note: BP-1..3 are labels added by us for referencing; CISA numbers them 1-3 without IDs. text_exact is copied verbatim (line wraps removed).

practices.text_exact: Use of unsupported (or end-of-life) software in service of critical infrastructure and national critical functions is dangerous and significantly elevates risk to national security, national economic security, and national public health and safety. This dangerous practice is especially egregious in technologies accessible from the internet.

Use of known/fixed/default passwords and credentials in service of Critical Infrastructure and national critical functions is dangerous and significantly elevates risk to national security, national economic security, and national public health and safety. This dangerous practice is especially egregious in technologies accessible from the internet.

practices.short: Single-factor authentication for remote or administrative access
practices.trigger: asset.remote_access == true and MFA not applied
practices.text_exact: The use of single-factor authentication for remote or administrative access to systems supporting the operation of Critical Infrastructure and national critical functions (NCF) is dangerous and significantly elevates risk to national security, national economic security, and national public health and safety. This dangerous practice is especially egregious in technologies accessible from the internet.
